summary: Built ObligationsRenewalPage (src/pages/ObligationsRenewalPage.jsx) as the full screen frame: breadcrumb (Home Page / Contract Repository / Contract Detail / Obligations & Renewal), header with contract name/counterparty/status and a top Amend/Terminate/Renew action group, the RenewalAlertPanel (gradient banner with the alert message, Contract End Date, Notice Period, and the Renew/Amend/Terminate buttons again, matching IMG-5), a 4-stat strip (Total/Completed/In Progress/Overdue), and the ObligationsTable with inline per-row edit (ObligationRowForm with Accept Suggestion + Save Changes, matching IMG-6's Edit Obligation panel) or ObligationsEmptyState + ManualObligationForm when extraction found nothing. Added ObligationsTabBlockedMessage for non-Executed contracts (UC9-AF-002) and ObligationsAccessDeniedView for roles outside Tenant Admin/Contract Owner/Legal Reviewer (UC9-AF-003, UC9-BR-012), with Legal Reviewer rendered read-only (hidden header actions, disabled in-banner actions, no Edit/Accept controls — UC9-BR-011). Wired every data path to the 8 listed endpoints via new contractRepositoryService.js functions, new feature hooks (useObligations, useCreateObligation, useUpdateObligation, useAcceptObligation, useRenewalPanel, useRenewContract, useAmendContract, useTerminateContract) and a new obligationsSlice zustand store. Added http.patch to the shared client (only PUT/POST/GET/DELETE existed before) since PATCH /obligations/{id} needed it. Routed at /contracts/:contractId/obligations and linked from ContractDetailPage's Obligations tab. Verified with lint (0 warnings), vitest (103/103 passing incl. 6 new ObligationsRenewalPage tests for loading/populated/empty-state/blocked/access-denied/read-only), a production build, and a live-rendered screenshot comparison against IMG-5 using a disposable local mock backend (not committed) — the populated screen (header, alert banner, stat strip, table rows, badge colors) visually matches IMG-5 closely. See blockers for TerminationReasonDialog ownership overlap, the inferred 'Active' status value, and the IMG-6 Contract Timeline widget that was not built.

pr.title: feat(ui-gen): build ObligationsRenewalPage
pr.body: Implements ObligationsRenewalPage (life-cycle-uc8-uc9 module) per UC9-MF-001/GC-001 and its AF/BR/FV stories: an obligations grid with inline edit + Accept Suggestion, a manual-add form for the extraction-found-nothing empty state, and a Renewal Alert panel with Renew/Amend/Terminate actions. Adds role gating (Tenant Admin/Contract Owner edit, Legal Reviewer read-only, everyone else denied) and a not-yet-Executed blocked state. See blockers for an ownership overlap with T-TERMINATION-REASON-DIALOG-UI and two inferred/omitted design details.

blockers: Task-ownership overlap: TerminationReasonDialog is listed under the separate T-TERMINATION-REASON-DIALOG-UI task's 'What you own' section, not this task's. Since that task's output did not exist yet and RenewAmendTerminateButtons' Terminate action (UC9-AF-001 AC6, UC9-BR-004, UC9-FV-001/002) is unusable without it, I implemented a minimal TerminationReasonDialog here (contractId, onClose, onConfirm props, matching the module skill's documented prop contract) so the page is actually testable end-to-end. If the other task also creates src/features/contract-repository/components/TerminationReasonDialog.jsx, the two will need to be reconciled/deduplicated by whichever lands second.

Inferred contract-status gating values: UC9-AF-002 requires hiding the tab until the contract is Executed, but ContractDetailResponse/ContractListItemResponse's documented status enum (Draft, In Negotiation, In Approval, In Signature, Executed, Expired, Terminated, Renewed, Amended) has no 'Active' value, even though the design (IMG-5) shows 'Status: Active' and several UC9 stories/business-rules refer to 'Executed or Active' contracts throughout. I treat status values Executed, Active, Renewed and Amended as unlocking this screen (EXECUTED_STATUSES in ObligationsRenewalPage.jsx) rather than only Executed, since the stories consistently pair the two; this is inferred, not confirmed against a backend enum.

Reused GET /api/v1/contracts/{contractId} (useContractDetail, already built for T-CONTRACT-DETAIL-PAGE-UI) to populate this page's header/breadcrumb (contract name, counterparty, status) and to gate on execution status, because this task's own 'relevant_endpoints' list does not include a contract-detail endpoint yet RenewalPanelResponse/ObligationResponse carry no contractName/counterparty/status fields the design's header requires. No new endpoint was invented — this is the same already-approved call ContractDetailPage uses.

IMG-6's right-hand 'Contract Timeline' panel (a 90/60/30-day alert history list with per-alert sent/due timestamps) was not built: RenewalPanelResponse only exposes a single alertThresholdDays value and renewalAlertBanner string, with no history array of past/future alert events to render that timeline from. I render only the fields the DTO provides (End Date, Notice Period, the current banner) and omitted the timeline widget rather than fabricate alert-history data.

BR-14's 'required evidence field' before marking an obligation Completed is referenced in the story notes as 'assumed to be an optional configurable field... not fully specified in the source document.' ObligationResponse does expose evidenceReference (nullable), and UpdateObligationRequest accepts it, but no UI control for entering/requiring it was added to ObligationRowForm beyond passing it through in the existing form fields, since neither the design images nor the DTO specify a dedicated evidence-upload field or where it should render.

Visual verification used a disposable local mock HTTP server (not committed, and not part of the app) standing in for the real backend, since no backend was running in this environment; .env.local was temporarily pointed at it and reverted afterward. Only the populated-list screen was screenshot-compared against IMG-5 (a close match); the IMG-6 inline edit panel was verified by reading the rendered component tree/tests rather than an interactive screenshot, since no headless browser automation library was available in this environment beyond the `npx playwright screenshot` CLI (which cannot click elements).
